judgments.reasoning_cat1: A no-consents representation whose only softness is the trailing 'except as contemplated herein or therein', a self-referential carve-out of uncertain reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel Clearwire representation in Section 6.03(b) instead carves out FCC spectrum-lease filings, and FCC approval is plainly needed for the IUAs, which sits awkwardly with this unqualified statement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Proceedings of general applicability and those related to market transitions' is a vague exclusion, and 'nor does there exist any basis therefore' is both a typo and an extraordinarily broad promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relies on Schedule 5.04 and on the knowledge standard fixed by Section 5.07, both of which fit; no contradiction located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision stacks 'only to the best knowledge', an assumption about third parties' compliance, and 'complied in all respects' against Material Adverse Effect qualifiers, producing a genuinely tangled standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.02 directs that Damages be computed 'without regard to any limitation or qualification as to materiality ... knowledge or similar language', which strips out precisely the qualifiers this representation depends on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line brokers representation; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 6.06 and conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'best knowledge after commercially reasonable investigation' including 'all facts which it knew or should have known' is a constructive-knowledge standard with a fuzzy boundary, but it is at least defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.02's instruction to disregard knowledge qualifiers in measuring Damages undercuts the utility of this definition, and no counterpart exists for Clearwire.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard good-standing representation; the reference to Clearwire as a 'foreign corporation' when it is an LLC is a minor slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes representations about Clearwire Parent, a Delaware corporation that the Preamble does not make a Party, leaving unclear who is answerable for them under Section 8.01(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate authorization and enforceability language; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states that Clearwire Parent has authority and defines 'Clearwire Documents' collectively, yet the enforceability sentence runs only against Clearwire, and Clearwire Parent is not a signing Party under the Preamble.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-conflict representation with enumerated heads and a materiality exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Unlike Section 5.03, it is not qualified by any schedule, but nothing elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear no-consents statement with an express FCC spectrum-lease filing carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same carve-out is duplicated verbatim at the end of Section 6.05, where it fits far less naturally; the duplication is untidy rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Litigation representation bounded by a materiality lead-in and a schedule; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Narrower than the Licensee's Section 5.04 counterpart, but asymmetry of this kind is a bargained allocation, not an internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'has complied in all respects' immediately qualified by a Material Adverse Effect exception is internally awkward, and the appended FCC filing carve-out is grafted onto a permits representation with stray punctuation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out repeats Section 6.03(b) and the materiality qualifier is nullified for damages purposes by Section 8.02; neither is a squarely contradictory provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line brokers representation; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 5.06; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'commercially reasonable efforts' to obtain consents 'required to be obtained by Clearwire and the Licensee' is broad, and the two sentences overlap confusingly on whose consents are whose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 5.03(b) and 6.03(b) represent that no consents are required except FCC filings, which sits oddly with a covenant to obtain a long list of consents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The duty is triggered by the party's own determination that a matter is 'reasonably likely to constitute a breach', a self-judging standard, but the mechanic is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imposes duties on Clearwire Parent, which the Preamble does not make a Party; otherwise it fits the indemnity structure of Article VIII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sprawling sentence with stacked provisos, an internal cross-reference to 'this sentence' that is hard to locate, and 'material risk' and 'knowingly or negligently' as the operative standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its opening limitation to 'spectrum that has not been subject to an IUA' is hard to square with the proviso making Clearwire responsible for the substantial-service requirement on licensed spectrum, and with Section 7.06's tax covenant running to spectrum under IUAs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section opens by limiting itself to spectrum not subject to an IUA, then closes with a general right to 'sell, assign, sublease, delegate or transfer this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations' to affiliates — a scope mismatch within one provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That closing sentence overrides the consent regime in the same section and is not reflected in Section 10.09's 'permitted assigns' language, leaving the assignment rules incoherent across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Parties believe that the provisions of this Agreement comply with all current FCC rules' followed by an agreement 'not to express any contrary view' is an unusual covenant of doubtful scope and enforceability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.03(a) contemplates jointly approaching the FCC for clarification when rules are disputed, which sits awkwardly with a promise never to express a contrary regulatory view.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all fees and taxes (now existing or hereafter arising) imposed on Licensee as a result of the licensing, regulation or use' with a non-exhaustive 'including, without limitation' list is a general catch-all against specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs 'until the end of the term of the IUA that is the last to expire', which extends well past the eighteen-month Term in Section 9.01, and overlaps Section 10.01's separate tax allocation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'act in a cooperative manner to preserve the intent of the relationships' and 'maintain that mutual advantage in accordance with the initial intent of the Parties' are about as vague as an operative covenant gets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A free-floating duty to preserve 'mutual advantage' can be invoked against almost any specific allocation in the Agreement, including Sections 1.02(b) and 2.02, but no single provision squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (iii) is a sweeping catch-all — 'or otherwise related to the activities of Clearwire, any of its Affiliates or any of its sublicensees or resellers including, without limitation, damage to health' — whose reach against the enumerated specifics is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has no counterpart in Licensee's indemnity at Section 8.01(a), and the internal lettering of Section 8.01(a) (which uses '(a)' and '(i)') breaks the cross-references in Section 8.03.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is deliberately expansive ('of every kind and description, contingent or otherwise') and includes items like 'statutory or regulatory compliance requirements' that are not obviously losses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its instruction to disregard materiality, Material Adverse Effect and knowledge qualifiers directly negates the qualifiers built into Sections 5.01, 5.05, 6.01 and 6.05 — a designed override, but one that leaves the representations' true content contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Headed as a limit on representation and warranty breaches, the operative text also captures 'the breach of any covenant', and the $10,000 Deductible is stated as a threshold that is then fully recoverable — internally confused.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites 'Section 8.01(a)(i)' and 'Section 8.01(b)(i)', but Section 8.01(a)'s sub-items are lettered '(a)' and '(i)', so the cross-reference does not map cleanly onto the indemnity it purports to limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but conventional claim-handling machinery; 'reasonably and promptly' and 'conflict or potential conflict' are soft but standard and procedurally bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'the Deductible referred to above', which Section 8.03 supplies, and works with Sections 8.01 and 8.04(c) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical notice-of-sums-due step; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Section 8.04(a) and does not conflict with the arbitration references elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear actual-prejudice rule for late notice; the standard is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the 'reasonably and promptly' notice duty in Section 8.04(a), which is exactly its intended function.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (3) defines the Term as ending when Licensee returns the unused Prepaid Royalties, which is circular given that the refund duty arises on expiration; the trailing 'except as it pertains to Puerto Rico' is unexplained and Clearwire's unilateral extension right cuts against fixed expiry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Section 2.02 (refund within five days after expiration, and Term not deemed expired while Option periods run), Section 1.02(d) (Options lapse on Term expiry) and Section 9.03 (Options survive) — those provisions cannot all be given full effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Event of Default' is defined by stacked vague terms — 'material obligation', 'material representation and warranty', and failure resulting in 'the inability of the other party to exercise its full rights' — and the second sentence about 'Loss' is unrelated to defaults.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.01 hangs termination rights on this definition, and it imports 'Loss (as defined in the applicable IUA)', a term that appears nowhere else in this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'obligations ... that by their nature would continue beyond expiration' is an inherently uncertain category, and the counterfactual 'or would have occurred, if Licensee complied in full' compounds it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves Options and rights of first refusal after termination, which directly contradicts Section 1.02(d)'s rule that outstanding Options lapse automatically on expiration of the Term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed enumerated tax list closed by 'or similar fees or taxes or governmental charges', a modest general-versus-specific tail.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Section 7.06's broader tax covenant without an ordering rule, and it indemnifies the 'Licensee(s) Indemnified Parties', a defined term drawn from Section 8.01(b) with a stray plural.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-year survival period running from either the Initial or a Subsequent Closing 'with respect to the EBS Spectrum that is subject to such ... Closing' is workable but the second sentence ('survive indefinitely until, by their respective terms, they are no longer operative') is close to self-cancelling.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.03 states a different survival rule by nature of the obligation, and Section 8.03's indemnity for representation breaches is not expressly tied to this one-year window.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard integration and non-waiver language, carefully drafted and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The integration clause covers 'this Agreement (including the schedules and exhibits hereto)' while the transaction also runs through IUAs, Collateral Documents and the Stock Pledge Agreement referenced in Sections 1.03 and 4.01(a) — leaving room to argue about what is integrated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain New York choice-of-law clause excluding renvoi; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing choice-of-law or forum term appears in the Agreement; Section 10.11 addresses procedure, not governing law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Headings-have-no-effect clause; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Useful here, since the table of contents mis-numbers many sections; it neutralises rather than creates conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The notice addressee is given as 'Clearwire Spectrum Holdings I LLC' rather than the 'II LLC' named in the Preamble, and the Kirkland, Washington addresses carry (415) area-code fax numbers — mechanical errors in the notice details themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The party-name discrepancy with the Preamble is the kind of mismatch that can be argued about when notice of default under Section 9.01 is at stake.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'to the extent possible' and 'reasonable time to comment' are soft, but the structure of the consent-plus-legal-exception is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No confidentiality section survives in the executed text to conflict with it (Section 11.14 appears only in the table of contents), so no operative clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare, one-sentence severability clause with no reformation or essential-terms proviso, so what happens when a central term fails is unaddressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Given the interlocking Option, refund and Term mechanics of Sections 1.02, 2.02 and 9.01, the absence of any carve-out makes its application uncertain, but no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, definite, though 'permitted assigns' presupposes an assignment-restriction that this section does not state.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The only assignment rules appear in Section 7.04, which is expressly limited to spectrum not subject to an IUA and yet contains a general right to transfer 'this Agreement' to affiliates — so what counts as a 'permitted assign' is not settled by the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stipulation that 'monetary damages alone will not be adequate' coupled with cumulative-remedies language is conventional, though the stipulation of irreparable harm for any refusal to perform is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves every remedy 'at law or in equity' notwithstanding any other provision, which pulls against Section 10.11's statement that the Dispute Resolution Procedures are the Parties' 'sole means' of resolving disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text breaks off mid-sentence at 'as their sole means of', so the operative scope of the exclusive dispute mechanism is literally incomplete — a mechanical defect on the face of the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A 'sole means' ADR provision has to be reconciled with Section 10.10's preservation of all legal and equitable remedies and with the arbitration references in Sections 1.04 and 3.03(b), which assume a fuller procedure than what survives here.
